findings.title: V2 now throws UnsupportedOperationException for legacy client operations that worked before.
findings.body: Before this change, `MgmtPermissionsV2.clients()` returned the V1 `ClientPermissions`. It now returns `ClientPermissionsV2`, where `canExchangeTo`, `isPermissionsEnabled`, `resource`, `getPermissions` and the `*Permission(client)` methods all throw `UnsupportedOperationException`. Any existing caller that reaches these with V2 enabled now gets a 500 instead of an answer. Examples: the legacy token-exchange provider calls `AdminPermissions.management(...).clients().canExchangeTo(...)`, and the client `management/permissions` admin endpoint calls `isPermissionsEnabled`. I could not see those callers, so please check them. For checks like `canExchangeTo`, return `false` (deny) instead of throwing. For the management endpoints, guard them with the V2 feature flag.

findings.title: A missing all-clients type resource causes a null dereference.
findings.body: If no resource exists for the client, the code loads the "Clients" type resource and passes it straight to `findByResource(server, resource)`. Nothing checks it for null first. Realms whose admin-permissions resource server was set up before the `Clients` type was added to the schema may not have that type resource. In those realms, every client permission check by an admin without `manage-clients` would throw a NullPointerException (or fail inside the store) instead of being denied. Add `if (resource == null) return false;` before the policy lookup.
